messages.author: 3d643362f888e7df
messages.subject: Obtain gradient inside model section
parts:
Hi

I'd like to know if it's possible to access the gradient of a quantity wrt. the parameters in the model section of a Stan file.

I understand Stan computes this as part of HMC, but I couldn't find any API in the reference.

Thank you,
Marmaduke

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Obtain gradient inside model section
parts:
No — this is tricky because it causes recursion in the autodiff
which would require nontrivial changes to the modeling language.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Obtain gradient inside model section
parts:
Yes, very tricky. The problem isn't the recursion per se,
so much as the staging. Our reverse-mode autodiff for gradients
builds up the entire expression graph then propagates the chain
rule backward. So the derivatives aren't available until after
the entire expression's built up and derivatives are propagated,
at which point, the model block's already been executed.

Going the other way, we'd very much like to be able to add in
a way for users to specify gradients for custom functions.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Obtain gradient inside model section
parts:
That’s what Riemannian HMC does.  Short story is that do to any
better than Euclidean HMC you need second _and_ third-order
derivatives.  It’s coming soon enough.
